europe.intro: The India half of this dashboard has an Atlantic mirror. The same warming baseline that inflates ENSO readings is loading Europe's summers — but the mechanism is physical, not a measurement artefact. This view tracks the Euro-Atlantic circulation regime that decides where the heat parks, and reads it against the ENSO chain.

hero.label: UK summer mean vs 1991–2020 (1 Jun–10 Aug)
hero.sub: On course for the UK's warmest summer on record — after the second-warmest June and second-warmest July. 2026 is the first UK year to hit 35°C in May, June and July.

mechanism.name: Omega Block · Heat Dome
mechanism.desc: A textbook Omega block: high pressure locked over core Europe with deep lows either side, over the North Atlantic and Russia. The high acts as a lid — sinking air compresses and warms, skies clear, the ground bakes day after day, and Saharan air is drawn north. The Atlantic flow that normally ventilates Europe is blocked.

regimes.name: European / Scandinavian Blocking
regimes.note: The active regime all summer — successive heat domes over Iberia, France and Central Europe. This is the pattern delivering the records.

regimes.name: Atlantic Ridge
regimes.note: Phases in as the block flexes west; keeps NW Europe and the northern British Isles nearer normal under maritime air.

regimes.name: NAO Positive
regimes.note: A zonal, Atlantic-driven regime would break the heat — largely absent this summer.

regimes.name: NAO Negative
regimes.note: Winter-relevant. The ENSO → Europe teleconnection strengthens from autumn; a strong El Niño tilts the odds of European winter circulation anomalies worth watching.

jet.desc: The jet stream is kinked into a stationary Omega, stalling systems for days at a time. With the Atlantic storm track deflected north, there is no westerly relief — the defining feature of a heat-dome summer, and the link from the tropical chain to the surface extreme.

europe.inference: Europe's warmest-summer-on-record trajectory is not primarily an ENSO story — the ENSO → Europe link is weak in summer and strongest in winter. It is a blocking story, amplified by a warmer baseline that lifts every heat-dome peak higher. That is the mirror of the India thesis: the measurement problem (the drifting ruler) and the physical problem (a blocking-prone, warming atmosphere) share one cause and must be read separately. The ENSO signal to watch here arrives with autumn, when the teleconnection to European winter circulation switches on.
